docs.title: Home
docs.text:
ProbingEnvironments

Find the bug in your RL agent without a long training run. Tiny environments with known answers: train your agent on one for a few thousand steps, and a wrong answer points at the part that is broken.

Install · Quickstart · The probes · Reading a failure · Connecting your agent · Documentation

A deep-RL agent that learns CartPole slowly, or not at all, can have a dozen causes, and some bugs hide others. ProbingEnvironments takes them apart. Each environment is small enough that the right value or action is known in closed form, and each one tests a single part of an actor-critic agent: the value loss, backpropagation, discounting, the policy update, the coupling between actor and critic, memory. Run them in order, and the first one that fails tells you where to look.

  • Known answers: the probes use one- and two-step episodes whose correct values and actions follow from the rules of the environment, with nothing to tune and no baseline to run.
  • Cheap: most checks train for a few thousand environment steps, seconds on a CPU, so they fit in a unit test suite and run on every change.
  • Two APIs: gymnax 1.0 environments for JAX agents (jit and vmap them with the agent), and Gymnasium ones for the rest.
  • Premade checks: each trains your agent through a small adaptor and fails with the expected and the measured value. An adaptor for Stable-Baselines3 is included, and a template shows how to write yours.

Ajax's probe suite is built on these environments.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install probing-environments
# with the premade Stable-Baselines3 adaptor
pip install "probing-environments[sb3]"

Version 0.6.0 and later need gymnax 1.0 or newer, and Python 3.11 to 3.14. To install main, whose documentation is the site's dev version:

pip install "git+https://github.com/YannBerthelot/ProbingEnvironments"

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Every snippet in this README runs as written: the test suite executes them (tests/test_readme.py).

docs.title: Check an agent
docs.text:
Each check trains the agent briefly on one environment and asserts that it reaches the known answer.

from stable_baselines3 import PPO

from probing_environments.adaptors.sb3 import (
    get_gamma,
    get_policy,
    get_value,
    init_agent,
    train_agent,
)
from probing_environments.checks import (
    check_actor_and_critic_coupling,
    check_advantage_policy,
    check_backprop_value_net,
    check_loss_or_optimizer_value_net,
    check_reward_discounting,
)

AGENT = PPO
BUDGET = 2_000  # environment steps per check

check_loss_or_optimizer_value_net(
    AGENT, init_agent, train_agent, get_value, budget=BUDGET
)
check_backprop_value_net(AGENT, init_agent, train_agent, get_value, budget=BUDGET)
check_reward_discounting(
    AGENT, init_agent, train_agent, get_value, get_gamma, budget=BUDGET
)
check_advantage_policy(AGENT, init_agent, train_agent, get_policy, budget=BUDGET)
check_actor_and_critic_coupling(
    AGENT, init_agent, train_agent, get_policy, get_value, budget=BUDGET
)

Put these calls in your unit tests and keep them there: they catch regressions as cheaply as they catch the first bug.

docs.title: Use an environment directly
docs.text:
The gymnax environments follow the gymnax 1.0 API: step returns six values, with a time limit reported as truncated, apart from terminated.

import jax

from probing_environments.gymnax_envs import RewardDiscountingEnv

env = RewardDiscountingEnv()
params = env.default_params
obs, state = env.reset(jax.random.PRNGKey(0), params)
obs, state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(
    jax.random.PRNGKey(1), state, 0, params
)

The discrete environments are in probing_environments.gymnax_envs, the continuous-action ones in probing_environments.gymnax_envs.continuous_actions and the Gymnasium ones in probing_environments.envs.

docs.title: The probes
docs.text:
Run them in this order: each assumes the ones before it pass. The checks train with a discount of γ = 0.5 (set by the check, or the adaptor's default). The discrete checks accept a value within 0.1 of the answer, or within 10% when that is larger.

Check Environment The agent must learn If it fails, look at 1 check_loss_or_optimizer_value_net ValueLossOrOptimizerEnv: one observation, one step, reward 1 V = 1 the value loss or the optimiser 2 check_backprop_value_net ValueBackpropEnv: observation 0 or 1, reward equal to it, one step V(0) = 0 and V(1) = 1 backpropagation through the value network 3 check_reward_discounting RewardDiscountingEnv: two steps, reward 1 at the end V(first) = γ and V(second) = 1 discounting and bootstrapping 4 check_advantage_policy AdvantagePolicyLossPolicyUpdateEnv: two actions, one step, action 0 pays more P(action 0) > 0.9 the advantage, the policy loss or the policy update 5 check_actor_and_critic_coupling PolicyAndValueEnv: a random observation, and the action that matches it pays the matching action with P > 0.9, and V = 1 for both observations the batching that feeds the networks, for example stale data in the value net 6 check_recurrent_agent RecurrentValueEnv (gymnax): the first observation, 0 or 1, is the reward two steps later V at the last step equals the first observation the memory, or how the hidden state is carried

Continuous-action agents run check_advantage_policy_continuous (the action must reach 0.9) and check_actor_and_critic_coupling_continuous (the action takes the sign of the observation, and V ≥ 0.8) on the continuous versions of probes 4 and 5. check_boundary_action_saturation asks more of probe 4: the action must reach 0.98 within its default 50,000 steps. An on-policy agent that recomputes log-probabilities by inverting its tanh stalls near 0.95.

TwoChoiceMDP (two reward cycles of gains 1/5 and 2/5) is there for average-reward agents. Its check, check_average_reward, is unfinished and does not run on the gymnax version.

docs.title: Reading a failure
docs.text:
A failing check raises AssertionError with the expected and the measured value. Probes 1 to 4 also name the part most likely at fault, for example "There is most likely a problem with your reward discounting".

  • Start from the first failing probe. A broken value loss can make later probes fail too, so their failures say little until it is fixed.
  • Read the measured value, not only the verdict. V = 2 on probe 1 means the agent bootstraps past the end of the episode; V = 0.5 on both observations of probe 2 means it does not see the observation.
  • Give it a larger budget before blaming a bug. A value that moves steadily towards the answer, but too slowly, points at the learning rate or the budget rather than at the code.

docs.title: Connecting your agent
docs.text:
A check drives your agent through a few functions, so it needs no change to your code:

Function What it does init_agent(agent, env, run_name, gamma, learning_rate, num_envs, budget) builds the agent on the probe environment class it is given train_agent(agent, budget) trains it for budget environment steps get_value(agent, obs) the critic's value of an observation get_policy(agent, obs) the action probabilities (discrete actions) get_action(agent, obs[, key]) the action, for continuous actions; the gymnax checks pass a PRNG key get_gamma(agent) the agent's discount factor init_hidden_state(), compute_next_critic_hidden(agent, obs, done, hidden), get_value_recurrent(agent, obs, done, hidden) the memory, for probe 6 only

probing_environments.adaptors.sb3 implements them for Stable-Baselines3. adaptors/template.py documents init_agent, train_agent, get_value, get_policy and get_gamma for writing your own; the continuous checks also need get_action, and a budget argument on init_agent. With an adaptor for a JAX agent, pass gymnax=True to a check to train on the gymnax version of its environment.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation site has this guide and the changelog, one version per release; dev follows main.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Planned for 0.7.0: environments that observe something informative and declare the action box they pay on, more probes (time limits, credit through a delayed reward, multi-dimensional actions, memory in the actor, stochastic rewards, average reward), and a report that names the likely cause from the probes' results.

docs.title: Related projects
docs.text:
• Debugging RL, Without the Agonizing Pain, Andy L. Jones: the idea and the first five probes come from this post.
  • bsuite: small experiments that measure an agent's capabilities, where these probes look for its bugs.
  • gymnax and Gymnasium: the two environment APIs implemented here.
  • Ajax: JAX agents whose probe suite is built on these environments.
  • TargetGym: setpoint-tracking environments with PID and MPC baselines, for when the probes pass.

docs.text:
Bug reports and new probes are welcome.

git clone https://github.com/YannBerthelot/ProbingEnvironments.git
cd ProbingEnvironments
uv sync
make ci   # pre-commit, the small and medium tests with coverage, the docs

make test runs only the fast tier.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Notable changes to ProbingEnvironments. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and versions follow semantic versioning.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text: • Characterization pins (tests/characterization/) record how every environment behaves today, through the API users and Ajax rely on. They keep the 0.7 refactor honest: a restructuring must leave them unchanged, and each deliberate behaviour change shows up as a pin difference with its own upgrade note here. No change to the package.

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.5.1
docs.text:
A minor release, because these changes break code written for 0.5.1:

  • gymnax 1.0 or newer is required. 0.5.1 required gymnax 0.0.9, so it could not be installed next to gymnax 1.x, and its environments failed on their first step under gymnax 1.0. Upgrade gymnax to >=1.0.
  • The gymnax environments follow the gymnax 1.0 API.
  • env.step returns six values, (obs, state, reward, terminated, truncated, info), instead of five. Unpack the extra value, and bootstrap your value targets at truncated steps: a time limit is no longer folded into done.
  • Environments implement is_terminated(state, params) instead of is_terminal. Rename it in your subclasses.
  • get_obs takes (state, params=None, key=None). Add the two optional arguments to your overrides.
  • The gymnax TwoChoiceMDP never terminates. Its episodes now end only at the time limit, reported as truncated, so an agent should bootstrap there.
  • pytest is no longer installed with this package. It moved to the development dependencies; add it to your own if you relied on it.
  • The Gymnasium environments draw from their own generator. reset(seed=s) seeds env.np_random, as Gymnasium specifies, instead of reseeding numpy's global generator, and a later reset() continues that stream. Seeded start observations no longer match 0.5.1's, where only the first one depended on the seed. If your code relied on reset seeding np.random, seed it yourself.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The sb3 extra: pip install "probing-environments[sb3]" installs Stable-Baselines3 for the premade adaptor.
  • A documentation site, versioned per release: https://yannberthelot.github.io/ProbingEnvironments/

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• jax, flax and numpy are declared as dependencies. The package imports them directly; before, they only arrived through gymnax.
  • six is declared: gymnax 1.0.1 imports it without declaring it, so a fresh install could not import the package.
  • Python 3.11 to 3.14 is supported; gymnax 1.0.1 supports Python below 3.15.
  • The package is built with hatchling and versioned from git tags. Release tags are now named vX.Y.Z; earlier ones had no v.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • probing_environments.adaptors.ajax warns on import and will be removed in 0.7.0. Ajax ships its own probe adaptor in its test suite.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • A seeded run through the SB3 adaptor is reproducible. The Gymnasium environments reseeded numpy's global generator from OS entropy on every automatic reset, so each run differed and the README's PPO example failed about once in 50 runs.
